design_note: Makes the critical path numerical without suggesting that parallel calls reduce total work. The reader sees one early result wait for a slower independent branch before synthesis can finish.

source.title: Building effective agents
source.publisher: Anthropic; Erik Schluntz and Barry Zhang
source.concept: Independent subtasks can execute in parallel and their results can be combined. Dependency structure determines which work can overlap.
source.scope: Original ShopAssist tools and timings; the source supplies the parallel-work principle, not these latencies or savings.

lesson.title: The slow branch sets the join time
lesson.intro: ShopAssist needs two authorized independent reads: stock takes 3 seconds and carrier status takes 5. Both start at 0; synthesis takes 1 second after both return. These are constructed timings.

data.result: Elapsed: max(3, 5) + 1 = 6 s; serial equivalent: 9 s.

read: Both reads start together because neither consumes the other result.
Stock finishing at 3 seconds does not make the combined answer ready.
The model can synthesize only after the slower result arrives at 5 seconds.
lesson.question: If stock takes 7 seconds instead, when does the answer finish under the same assumptions?
lesson.answer: At 8 seconds: max(7, 5) + 1. The stock branch becomes the critical path. Parallelism overlaps independent work; it does not remove the need to perform or pay for both reads. Quota contention, retries or extra joining overhead would require a different timing model.
lesson.takeaway: Follow dependencies to calculate elapsed time; count all work separately for cost.
lesson.assumption: Constructed timings; ample capacity, simultaneous dispatch, no failures, and zero dispatch/join overhead. Diagram spacing represents order, not duration.
